The flute version of [Patterns by Ear](patterns-by-ear.qmd). The first few patterns of a set are taught with fingering diagrams.
Then the page plays the rest, one at a time, and you play each back on your flute. New to the fingerings? See the
[fingering chart](../lessons/flute.qmd#fingering-chart).

## By ear {#by-ear}

```{=html}
<div class="ep-panel">
  <div class="ep-dots" id="ef-dots2"></div>
  <div class="ep-head" id="ef-ear-head">Learn the first patterns, then come here.</div>
  <div class="ep-solf" id="ef-ear-solf"></div>
  <div class="ef-fings" id="ef-ear-fing"></div>
  <div class="ep-msg" id="ef-ear-msg" aria-live="polite"></div>

    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-primary" id="ef-ear-hear">🔊 Hear it again</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ef-ear-key">Hear the key</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ef-ear-show">Show me</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="ef-ear-skip">Skip</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" id="ef-ear-next" hidden>Next ▶</button>
  </div>
  <p class="ep-muted">The key is played first (I – V7 – I). Then each pattern: listen, then play it back. A wrong note stops the
  try and the pattern plays again. "Show me" and running out of tries count as a miss.</p>
</div>
```

## How it works {#how}

- **Written notes.** The flute does not transpose: the notes on your part are the notes you hear, so the page plays and listens at
  the pitch you play, and no instrument needs choosing. (Many notes use the same fingers an octave apart: the octave is air and lips,
  and *Any octave counts* is on by default.)
- **Range.** Each set is moved to the key you pick and placed between D4 and D6, in the flute's first two octaves, when it fits.
- **Fingerings.** The usual fingering from the [fingering chart](../lessons/flute.qmd#fingering-chart). Your teacher may prefer an
  alternate (for example the B♭ thumb key or the side lever for B♭).
- **What counts.** The notes in order; rhythm isn't checked. Each new note must hold steady for about a tenth of a second. To play the
  same note twice, stop the sound briefly between them (tongue it). With *Any octave counts* on, the whole pattern may be an octave away.
  Stopping for more than four seconds starts the try again.
- **The microphone** ignores everything while the page is playing. Headphones still help: a loud room can confuse it.
- **No flute handy?** A MIDI keyboard or wind controller, or the computer keys, count as written notes.
